cards.text: The LORD is still talking with Moses, Israel's leader, about the tabernacle (Exodus 25:1). Now He turns from the tent to people. He tells Moses to have his brother Aaron brought to him from among the Israelites, along with Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

cards.question: Aaron and his four sons are brought to Moses to serve God as ___.

cards.text: Then God turns to clothes. He tells Moses to make holy garments for his brother Aaron.

cards.question: God tells Moses to make holy garments for Aaron. What are they meant to give him?
Moses isn't sewing these himself. Who does God tell him to instruct to make Aaron's garments?
God says He filled the skilled craftsmen making Aaron's garments with a spirit of ___.

cards.text: God lists the garments: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. SIX pieces? That's not an outfit, friend, that's a whole closet.

cards.question: God says the six holy garments are just for Aaron and nobody else.

cards.text: They'll use gold, fine linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and the ephod comes first, with two shoulder pieces and a woven waistband made all in one piece. That's ONE piece, friend, with no shortcuts and no 'eh, close enough.'

Then God tells Moses to engrave the names of the sons of Israel, the man once called Jacob (Genesis 32:28), on two onyx stones, six to a stone, the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. As a stamper whose stamps used to come out blurry, I'm a LITTLE jealous.

cards.question: God says Aaron carries the names of the sons of Israel on his two shoulders as a ___ before the LORD.

cards.text: Then come gold filigree settings and two chains of pure gold, braided like cord and attached to the settings. Braided GOLD, friend, and I can't even braid dough without it looking like it lost a fight.

Next up, the breastpiece of judgment, made like the ephod with gold, colored yarn and fine linen, and square when folded double. Then come four rows of gemstones set in gold, from a ruby, a topaz and an emerald in the first row to a beryl, an onyx and a jasper in the fourth. TWELVE gemstones, friend, and I'd be too scared to sneeze anywhere near it.

cards.question: Each of the twelve stones on the breastpiece is engraved with the name of one of the twelve ___.

cards.text: Then come braided chains of pure gold and gold rings, fastening the breastpiece's corners to the shoulder pieces of the ephod. That breastpiece has more gold hardware than my whole bakery, friend.

cards.question: The rings of the breastpiece get tied to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn. What does God say that's for?

answers.text: So it does not swing out from the ephod
So Aaron can untie it quickly
So it sits below the waistband

cards.text: Now here's the part I love. In the Holy Place, Aaron carries the names of the sons of Israel on that breastpiece.

cards.question: Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he carries the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece over his ___.
The names on the breastpiece are a reminder before the LORD only on Aaron's first day as priest.

cards.text: Then God tells Moses to place the Urim and Thummim on Aaron's outfit too.

cards.question: God tells Moses to place the Urim and Thummim so they'll also be over Aaron's heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Where do they go?

cards.text: God says Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD. Not tucked in a back pocket, friend. Right up CLOSE.

Next is the robe of the ephod, entirely blue cloth, with a woven collar around the opening at the top so it won't tear. Everybody who's ever heard that little RRRIP pulling a shirt over their head just stood up and clapped.

Around the lower hem go pomegranates made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with gold bells between them, taking turns all the way around. My Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, is shaped like a bell, and just ONE of her could fill a whole kitchen with noise. A whole HEM of them?

cards.question: Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and God says its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD. What reason does God give?

answers.text: So that he will not die
So the people will bow down
So the elders will gather near

cards.text: Then God tells Moses to make a plate of pure gold and engrave words on it like a seal.

cards.question: What does God tell Moses to engrave on the plate of pure gold?
A blue cord fastens the gold plate to the front of Aaron's ___.

cards.text: That gold plate is to be on Aaron's forehead always. God says it's so Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things the Israelites consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts.

cards.question: Aaron bears the iniquity of the Israelites' holy gifts with that gold plate on his forehead. What does God say it's for?

answers.text: So they may be acceptable before the LORD
So Aaron may rule over all the tribes
So the people may never sin again

cards.text: Aaron gets a fine linen tunic, a fine linen turban and an embroidered sash, and his sons get tunics, sashes and headbands. The whole family's coordinated, friend, and you KNOW how hard it is to get two people to match for one family photo.

cards.question: God says only Aaron's garments, and not his sons', are meant to give glory and splendor.
Once the garments are on Aaron and his sons, God tells Moses to anoint them, ordain them and consecrate them.

cards.text: Last come linen undergarments, from waist to thigh. Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar, so that they will not incur guilt and die.

cards.question: God gives a rule for Aaron and his sons about wearing linen undergarments whenever they minister. He says it's to be a ___ statute for Aaron and his descendants.

cards.text: That's every last stitch of Aaron's outfit. But hold on to your apron, friend, because God's not done talking to Moses yet.
